isolation: Each scenario acquired its own fresh OAuth2 authorization_code+PKCE token via a sign-in through Thunder SSO's hosted login UI (driven with agent-browser) as the project's single provisioned test account, test-caller. The one UI-bearing step is that sign-in; the hello-api itself has no UI, so the When/Then of every scenario was driven directly against the deployed API with curl, each call read independently rather than depending on prior app state. The negative scenario simply omitted the Authorization header. The fixed-greeting scenario modeled Sam and Jordan as two independent sign-in sessions on the same test account (only one is provisioned), and compared the two responses directly rather than against a stored total, so the assertion holds regardless of any other traffic hitting the deployed app concurrently.

scenarios.rule: Only a signed-in caller may request the greeting
scenarios.scenario: A signed-in caller receives the greeting
